    Proposition 6.1: residual correction spaces #

    positive-deformations.tex (prop:residual-correction-spaces). In characteristic two, under the brick hypothesis, call a periodic component residual if ⊕_m coker D_m(C) has a nonzero class supported on it. Then each residual component is ℤΔ/⟨τ^{s_i}ρ⟩ with Δ of type D or E, there is a path p_i : τ v_i → v_i of degree d_i = 2s_i + 2, and ⊕_{m≥2} coker D_m(C) = ⊕_{i∈I} k[p_i].

    The spanning by at most one row per periodic component is residual_cokerSpan. Here:

    • the mesh derivative commutes with the projection to a union of components of a quiver (D_projA), so the image of D is stable under it (projM_mem_imageD);
    • after the localization of Proposition 5.1 to the periodic vertices (where periodic components are unions of connected components), a family supported on one periodic component lies in the image of D as soon as it does modulo families supported elsewhere (mem_imageD_of_supported);
    • hence rows in distinct periodic components with nonzero classes are linearly independent (rows_independent).

            Proposition 6.1 (prop:residual-correction-spaces). In characteristic two, for a finite-dimensional scalar mesh category on a finite translation quiver with at most one arrow between ordered vertices, satisfying the brick hypothesis, there is a set S of rows p_i at periodic vertices, at most one in each periodic component, such that:

            • the classes [p_i] span ⊕_{m≥2} coker D_m(C), are nonzero, and are linearly independent (so ⊕_{m≥2} coker D_m(C) = ⊕_i k[p_i]);
            • a periodic component is residual exactly when it carries a row of S (so S is indexed by the residual components I);
            • the component of each p_i is ℤΔ/⟨τ^{s_i}ρ⟩ with Δ of type D or E, ρ fixing the centre, and p_i has degree d_i = 2s_i + 2 (StarTrace.DEModel; in particular d_i is the only degree of a nonzero class on the component);
            • the rows are killed by two over every coefficient ring (used for Lemma B.2).
